(d) the @ConditionalOnBean ordering + resolver-vs-cache gating is now a recorded opa-abac pattern; planning should pin the exact auto-config condition when an advice depends on a conditionally-produced bean. QA: a /deep-review has not yet run (phase ④ next); the run's own ★ gates + the live e2e + the full coexistence sweep caught everything above, so no laziness signal so far — the two substantive bugs (missing bulk, empty-map) were caught by the MANDATORY live e2e, which is exactly why the flow mandates it.

name: Run: B3 cross-service HTTP resilience (4 tickets)
description: OUTCOME: paused-and-asked ONCE (T2), otherwise a clean autonomous run; full ./gradlew build green, the live e2e headline passed (E1 200 / E2 403). PAUSE-CAUSE (class: 'undecided externally-visible behavior the design left unpinned', T2): the OPA decorator wraps the OpaClient INTERFACE, but HttpOpaClient swallows every failure into its fail-closed value and never throws — so for allow/allowAll the decorator cannot distinguish a transient failure from a genuine policy deny (compile is clean: fromError distinguishes error() from a real denyAll()). The decomposition's open notes flagged the e2e stub question but did NOT pin how allow/allowAll detect a failure to retry. Surfaced via AskUserQuestion; the maintainer chose retry-on-the-fail-closed-sentinel (retry allow on false / allowAll on any-false), accepting one extra ~50ms sidecar hop on a deny (deterministic -> still false, never widens) for the transient-recovery headline. CHECKPOINT/TICKET FRICTION: (a) T2 build-breaker landed in-commit — the BeanPostProcessor wraps a USER-supplied OpaClient too, breaking the existing userBeansWin() type assertion (fixed: run it resilience-off + add a wrap-the-user-bean test). (b) T3 build-breaker landed in-commit — the new 4-arg (…,CallGuard) constructor made each @Component edge ambiguous (two public ctors); fixed with @Autowired on the production ctor. (c) T1 R4j gotcha: CircuitBreaker.of() has no Clock overload in R4j 2.x; the only clock-injection seam is the public internal.CircuitBreakerStateMachine(name,cfg,clock) ctor. (d) T4 rig gotchas discovered LIVE (class: rig/test-harness gotcha): the protected route is NESTED /catalogs/{id}/categories/{id} not flat; the psql fixture needs NOT-NULL created_at+tags+ltree path; profile.sh up must precede deploy.sh up. PLANNING-GAP->FIX: (1) the OPA-decorator retry-signal was the keystone unpinned semantic — a future 'decorate a fail-closed-swallowing client' slice should pin IN DESIGN how the decorator detects failure-vs-legitimate-deny when the delegate never throws (the fromError-vs-false asymmetry across the three methods). grill-me should ask 'if the wrapped call swallows failures, what is the retry signal, and does retrying the fail-closed value re-run legitimate denies?'. (2) T4's fixture-seed schema + the exact protected URL should be pinned in 10-QA-TEST-CASES so the e2e runner is right first time (the naive seed + flat URL both failed live). QA: no post-run /deep-review yet (recommended next, flow phase ④); the run's own gates (unit+IT+ the live e2e two-pass) caught everything in-loop.

name: Run: B3 — deep-review QA close-out
description: Closes the QA field of the B3 run retro (mx-31ec93, which recorded 'no post-run /deep-review yet'). The /deep-review (multi-lens adversarial, 8 lenses + refutation + completeness critic, 12 agents) found 0 Critical and 0 fail-open/widening/concurrency defects, but DID surface ONE genuine Medium the run's own ★ gate + green tests MISSED: the OPA circuit breaker counted genuine policy DENIALS as failures (the decorator retries on the deny-sentinel, which fed breaker.onError) → ~3 consecutive deny requests self-open the breaker → it then force-denies otherwise-ALLOWABLE requests for 10s. NOT a fail-open (outcome stays fail-closed) but a self-inflicted availability regression violating the slice's own ADR 0017 §5 'never a decision input'. WHY THE RUN MISSED IT (the laziness/self-preferential-bias signal): the issue sits INSIDE the design decision the run made (retry-on-fail-closed-sentinel, settled mid-run), and the ONLY breaker-open test drove the breaker via the deny sentinel itself — so the run's own test masked the bug rather than exposing it. The completeness critic (not the lens fan-out, not refutation) is what raised it. LESSON for the autonomous flow: when a slice's design decision introduces a new way to feed a shared component (here: a retry heuristic that also records breaker failures), the run's own acceptance test for that component must exercise the DISTINGUISHING case (genuine-deny-stays-closed), not just the happy fault path — otherwise the gate is satisfied literally by the defective code. Fixed in commit 0b9c38b (breaker records only on the thrown-fault path) + the L1 decision-path test; full note docs/code-review/B3-HTTP-RESILIENCE-REVIEW.md. Merged to main via PR #43 (squash 5f8fd0f). Outcome of the run is now: partial (one mid-run pause) + one post-review Medium = the deep-review earned its keep.

PLANNING-GAP -> FIX (keystone): phase-① grill-me should have asked, for ANY fallback-removal slice: 'which type-level @OpaPreAuthorize gates lose their role when the fallback is removed under app-resolved roles (list AND create AND tag-on-create), AND which matrix SETUPS create fixtures via that fallback?' Pre-resolving those two questions in design converts this paused run into a full-success. Add to the slice's 00-DESIGN blast-radius: enumerate type-level gates + fixture-creation paths, not just the headline data-row path. name: Slice size is the lever: decompose so each slice's blast-radius fits one head
description: MAINTAINER'S CALL (2026-06-30, after the B4 run): the recurring autonomous-run pause class — 'design left a fail-open/contract semantic unpinned' (mx-7e0a17) — is itself largely a SYMPTOM OF SLICE SIZE, not just of grill-me depth. B4 was 9 tickets spanning a new library annotation seam (@OpaPreAuthorize roleResource), two services (catalog + user-mgmt), the APISIX gateway, AND a rewrite of a load-bearing policy clause (the realm-fallback removal). At that size the blast-radius analysis (00-DESIGN phase ①) CANNOT stay complete in one pass — which is exactly why the three type-level-gate regressions slipped through to the e2e. RULE: prefer decomposing into 2-3 smaller slices, each with a blast-radius small enough to FULLY enumerate during grill-me, over one large slice with a partial blast-radius. Heuristic smells that a slice is too big and should be split BEFORE writing the autonomous prompt: (a) it both REMOVES/CHANGES a load-bearing shared mechanism AND adds new surface that depends on it (B4: removed the fallback + added the governed-scope/ownership self-service) — split the removal+its-fix from the new feature; (b) it crosses >1 deployable (library + service + gateway) in one prompt; (c) the ticket count is >~5-6; (d) phase ① can't name every consumer of a mechanism it changes. The fail-open/contract questions (mx-7e0a17) are still the thing to pin — but a smaller slice makes pinning them tractable instead of aspirational. PRACTICAL SPLIT B4 SHOULD HAVE BEEN: (1) isolation-only = the filter entrypoint + fallback removal + the type-level-gate role-resolution fix, proven by the isolation matrix + a re-run of the existing suite; (2) self-service = ownership SPI + createTeam + gateway routing. Each ~4-5 tickets, each blast-radius enumerable. This feeds phase ② (/decompose): when sizing a slice, apply smells (a)-(d) and split rather than accept a 9-ticket prompt.

name: QA addendum: Run B4 — deep-review findings vs the run's own gate
description: QA addendum to the B4 MULTI-TENANT-ISOLATION run retro (the post-run /deep-review the original record said had not yet run). The 8-lens adversarial review found 4 issues (2 Medium, 2 Low, 0 Critical) the run's own e2e gate missed — answering the domain's 'did a post-run /deep-review find what the run missed?' QA question: YES, two of substance. (1) M1 SECURITY: /internal/catalog/{id}/created-by was reachable through the gateway catch-all (creator-sub leak) — the run's e2e exercised everything THROUGH the gateway but never PROBED /internal through the gateway, so the leak was invisible to it; an e2e that asserts the happy path can't see a negative-space exposure. PLANNING-GAP->FIX: the slice's QA cases should include an explicit 'every /internal/* path returns 404 through the gateway' assertion whenever a slice adds an /internal endpoint behind a catch-all gateway. (2) M2 TEST_GAP: the type-level-gate tests asserted the gate's SHAPE via the id-OMITTED input, not the production CUT via the real id:null wire shape — the signature autonomous laziness mode (assert shape, not the actual cut). The fix's own unit tests passed without testing the fix. FIX: when a fix turns on a serialization detail (null vs absent, scalar vs array), the regression test MUST use the real wire shape, and should be proven to fail when the fix is reverted. (3+4) Low: an undocumented 403 in the OpenAPI spec + an untested fail-closed disjunct (subject==null). NET: the run was solid (0 Critical, fail-closed/core-boundary/residual-AND all held), but the e2e-as-sole-gate let a Medium security leak and a Medium test-gap through — reinforcing that a post-run /deep-review is a REQUIRED phase-④ step, not optional, especially for a slice that adds gateway routes + a serialization-sensitive policy clause. name: Workflow subagent context: what a spawned agent actually inherits (probed, not assumed)
description: Probed 2026-07-31 with two independent agents, agreeing on every point. WHAT A WORKFLOW SUBAGENT GETS: (a) PARENT CONVERSATION - nothing. No turns, no summary, no prior findings; only the prompt string. (b) global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md + the cwd-level project CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md - PRE-INJECTED verbatim before any tool call. (c) the REPO-LOCAL CLAUDE.md (the one carrying the IP boundary, commit identity, Mulch domain table) - NOT pre-injected; it arrives lazily only after the agent first touches that directory. (d) Mulch - fully reachable (ml on PATH, store resolves, real records return) but NOTHING AUTO-PRIMES: the parent ml prime lives in the parent context only; what IS pre-injected is prose ABOUT Mulch (the habit + the --budget trap), not records. (e) the vault and the whole workspace tree - freely readable, inside and outside the repo. AUTHORING CONSEQUENCES: (1) CARRY FACTS, FETCH CORPORA - paste known facts into the prompt (the seam auditors got exact jar paths, not go-find-them); make an agent prime only when reasoning over a whole domain IS its job, and pass --budget 8000 INSIDE that prompt since the truncation trap applies to subagents too. (2) RESTATE THE BOUNDARIES - never assume the clean-room rule / commit identity / read-only posture reached the agent; the file carrying them is precisely the one not pre-injected. (3) AGENTS REPORT, THE PARENT RECORDS - parallel agents writing one Mulch store race on the same file and multiply the swept-staged trap. SIDE-FINDINGS: reading a CLAUDE.md RE-INJECTS its whole content as a system-reminder (touching a dir with one is not free); and anything in the global CLAUDE.md is in EVERY subagent context from its first token - which is why the corp tokens were moved to the macOS keychain the same day.

PAUSE-CAUSE (both pauses, one class): "a third-party seam named from a mental model" - the decomposition named a tools/list filter hook, an extract(Jwt) signature, a rule-qualified policy path, and a descriptor field, four APIs that sounded right and did not exist as written. T4 also paused on the principal-ceiling shape (design fork the docs did not cover). PLANNING-GAP -> FIX (all mechanized 2026-07-31, not left as advice): (a) seam-verification is now a ticket rule + two seam-existence audit angles; (b) acceptance-citation cross-reference is now a script (first run found 17 broken citations + 35 uncited QA cases in a package that had passed every prior gate, incl. a phantom P1-P10 series); (c) the unpinned-semantics critic; (d) the retrospective domain and the documentation delta were both promoted from per-repo SLOTS to invariants after both were found to be consumed-by-two-phases and produced-by-nothing. QA: an adversarial validation pass over the amended package returned 19 confirmed / 24 refuted, its headline being that OpaClient.allowAll is contractually TOTAL so T5s degradation trigger could never fire and an OPA outage would have produced the empty roster the design forbade - a defect in text written the previous day and already reviewed by two ad-hoc auditors. THE GENERALIZABLE HABIT: the T5 grill answered its biggest question by MEASUREMENT (a lab spike over real HTTP) rather than debate, and the measurement DELETED a hard prerequisite (the custom contextExtractor) instead of confirming it. An afternoon of spiking retired an assumption that would otherwise have been built on.

name: Run: AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ T5-T6 (the finish; slice complete)
description: OUTCOME: success - T5 and T6 shipped with NO pause to ask; the only interruption was a context-budget handoff the maintainer chose, not a fork the docs could not answer. PAUSE-CAUSE: none. FRICTION (two, and they are the SAME class as this slice's earlier two pauses - 'a third-party seam behaving differently from the mental model of it', which is why the 2026-07-31 gates were built): (1) T5's protocol flip to STREAMABLE turned tools/list into an ASYNC dispatch, and the stateless Spring Security chain denied the re-dispatch AFTER the handler had completed - aborting a half-written chunked body instead of returning 403. Fixed with dispatcherTypeMatchers(ASYNC, ERROR).permitAll(). Only a REAL POST /mcp finds this; a 401-before-routing test never can. (2) T6's rig found two defects the green unit+IT suites could not: the type-level ceiling asked governed-targets for the REQUESTED type while membership lives on the governing ROOT (ADR 0018), so ?resourceType=product was empty for someone who may read every product they govern - the tool surface REMOVED REST access and erased the slice's headline; and Spring AI's annotation-scanned call handler CATCHES what an @McpTool method throws and flattens it, so the PEP's own catch never fires in the real path and a target-gate denial arrived unlabelled. Both unit tests passed throughout because their fixtures build the specification with a straight-through handler. PLANNING-GAP -> FIX: the gates WORKED where they had been mechanized - the adversarial pass caught the missing APISIX route (catalog-all /* already matches /mcp) and the buildContext gate-off seam BEFORE implementation, and it found I27 unsatisfiable (fix-until-green had no reachable green state). The residual gap is narrower and specific: seam-verification was applied to SIGNATURES (does this API exist?) but not to SEMANTICS (does this API do what the name implies when it is in the real invocation path?). Concrete fix for the next decomposition: for every third-party seam a PEP composes with, the ticket must name ONE end-to-end assertion that runs through the REAL adapter, not a hand-built fixture - the two T6 defects and the T5 ASYNC defect are all instances of a fixture that was shaped like the seam rather than being it. QA: the post-run gate is /deep-review (maintainer-run). The run's own gates: gradle build green, :example-mcp-server:test 129, opa test 264/264, local Sonar 41 findings / 0 real, the new agent matrix 49 requests / 73 assertions / 0 failures first try, and the pre-existing fleet 14/14 on documented rig flavours.

name: QA addendum: what /deep-review found on AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ after the run's own gates were green
description: The run's retrospective recorded outcome=success on its own gates (build, 129 tests, opa 264/264, Sonar 0 real, the e2e matrix green first try). A post-run /deep-review then found 14 confirmed issues, 0 Critical — so the honest QA answer for that run is PARTIAL, and this is the record that says so. WHAT THE RUN'S GATES STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT SEE, which is the reusable part: (1) A COHERENCE defect — two readers of one kill-switch, each defensible alone, that together inverted the design's own roster-vs-call-path invariant and falsified three shipped statements. No single-file review finds this; you have to enumerate every reader of a switch and diff their interpretations AGAINST EACH OTHER. (2) A Rego truthiness fail-open (actor=false escaping to the human branch) that 264 passing policy tests missed because no test supplied a BOOLEAN for a field everything else supplies as a string — the test corpus mirrored the PEP's output shape rather than the policy's input space. (3) A load-bearing seam with ZERO tests (TypeLevelRoleDefinitionSupplier — one of the tool-gate's two inputs) that no coverage gate flagged, and which is exactly where the rig had already found a defect mid-run. (4) TWO assertions that could not fail: a gate-off roster test whose stub allowed every tool, and an 'OFF is never wider than ON' cell where the downstream denied for an independent reason. PLANNING-GAP -> FIX: the decomposition's ticket-level acceptance is per-ticket, so a seam added LATE by a gate (the buildContext gate-off parameter, added by the adversarial pass between T4 and T5) gets no acceptance case of its own and no cross-reader check — add 'every reader of a new switch/flag agrees' as an explicit acceptance line whenever a ticket introduces one. PROCESS NOTE for the next workflow invocation: the Workflow tool's 'args' input must be a JSON VALUE, not a JSON-encoded string — passing a string silently left args.base and args.focus undefined, so the review ran against a stale local 'main' and without the focus steer (coverage was unaffected — the lenses are failure-mode-based — but the prioritised surfaces had to be hand-verified).

name: Ground the grill in the code before asking the fork - research-phase recommendations decay against a moving codebase
description: SUPERVISOR-STEP-UP phase ① (2026-08-01) measured this: of the research brief's recommended answers, THREE were wrong and two of the eventual load-bearing forks were absent from the agenda entirely - and every one of those five was surfaced by a targeted code read taking a couple of minutes, not by discussion. The grill-me skill's own instruction ('if a question can be answered by exploring the codebase, explore the codebase instead') is therefore not a shortcut for cheap questions, it is the mechanism that keeps a research brief honest: a brief written N weeks earlier encodes assumptions about mechanisms that have since shipped, been renamed, or turned out to work differently than the web sources implied. Concretely, the reads that paid: grep the precedent a design claims to copy (abac_deny turned out to be protected by ABSENCE, not by a rule); read the cross-service PROJECTION not just the entity (TagDefinitionView silently drops the flag the design wanted to lean on); read the actual controller annotations (child lists already carry roleResourceType/roleResourceId, so the governing root is free there); read the record the design wants to widen (ParentRef is (type,id) and the resolvers never load entities); and check whether the infrastructure a fork assumes even EXISTS (there is no audit-event infrastructure at all - only @EnableJpaAuditing - so 'first-class audit events' was build-from-zero, not a yes/no). The generalization for phase ①: for each fork on the agenda, first identify the ONE file that would falsify the brief's recommendation, and read it. Budget the grill's questions for what code cannot answer - values, tolerances, blast-radius appetite - and let the codebase answer everything else. A brief's 'settled' list is safe to ratify; its 'recommended' answers are hypotheses.

name: Capability spike: subagent-delegation environment (umbrella cwd), 2026-08-01
description: Measured 2026-08-01 in the live session environment (session cwd = the umbrella workspace ~/Workspace/ai-engineering, which is NOT a git repo) before designing parts-orchestration for the autonomous runner. Two synchronous probes (subagent_type=general-purpose and =claude), IDENTICAL results - no roster variance this day. (1) Skill IS invocable inside a spawned subagent - proven live, a user-global skill loaded its content on request. (2) Workflow tool is ABSENT inside subagents (both probes) - a multi-agent review layer cannot run inside a delegated part; any heavier fan-out review must run from the MAIN session after parts complete. (3) Agent tool IS present inside subagents - nesting exists but is untested; do not build on it. (4) Main-session Agent tool runs subagents in the BACKGROUND by default - run_in_background=false is the load-bearing override whenever sequential parts share one branch/worktree. (5) Context injection into a subagent: user-global CLAUDE.md YES; cwd-level (umbrella) CLAUDE.md YES; the persistent-memory MEMORY.md YES; but a NON-cwd repo's CLAUDE.md does NOT inject - the probe could not name this repo's commit-identity email. A per-part brief must therefore restate every repo-local rule it depends on (commit identity, clean-room boundary, the ml-sync staged-sweep trap). (6) Subagent roster gaps vs the main session: no Grep, no Glob, no TaskCreate, no AskUserQuestion - a part-runner CANNOT ask the user, so escalation must travel via greppable on-disk markers collected by the orchestrator; file search is Bash-only. (7) THE LOCAL TRAP: project-scoped skills (this repo's .claude/skills) ARE listed and DO resolve inside subagents even from the umbrella cwd, BUT a skill whose dynamic preamble derives the repo root from the current directory (cd to git rev-parse --show-toplevel) FATALS with 'not a git repository' because a fresh shell starts at the umbrella root. The MAIN session masks this only because its persistent shell happens to be cd'd into the repo from earlier commands - so the failure is invisible until the first delegated run. Any runner skill, part brief, or gate script must pin the repo path EXPLICITLY (an absolute cd as step 0), never derive it from an assumed-repo cwd.

name: Gate recovery: resuming an interrupted validation workflow (SUPERVISED-SCOPE, 2026-08-01)
description: A 41-agent decompose-validation run died mid-flight on a session limit: 37 agents errored INCLUDING EVERY VERIFIER, and the workflow still returned counts {confirmed:0,refuted:0} — indistinguishable from a clean pass unless the agent-error tally is read alongside it. RECOVERY THAT WORKED, in order: (1) read the run's journal.jsonl - per-agent result rows survive the failure, so the 4 completed audit agents' 37 candidate findings were recoverable without re-running anything; (2) hand-verify the single highest-severity candidate immediately (here an opa eval), because one confirmed run-stopper is enough to block the package regardless of what the rest say; (3) after the limit reset, probe capacity with ONE trivial haiku subagent before relaunching a 41-agent fan-out; (4) relaunch with resumeFromRunId + the IDENTICAL args - the completed audit agents replay from cache instantly and only the errored verifiers run live (measured: 41/41 done, 0 errors, second attempt). OUTCOME DELTA that proves why the vacuous pass matters: the same package that scored confirmed:0 when broken scored 20 confirmed / 17 refuted (2 run-stoppers, 8 contradictions, 10 nits) when actually run. Generalize: for ANY multi-agent gate, treat (agents_error>0 AND confirmed==0) as NOT-RUN and re-run; never let a truncated fan-out's counts stand as evidence.

description: OUTCOME full-success — first real ORCHESTRATOR-mode run (post-PARTS-PORT): part 0 (T1–T3) and part 1 (T4–T6) each completed autonomously in a fresh-context subagent, all disk-collection checks green first try, zero escalations, zero mid-run pauses; the only maintainer touch was the pre-declared part-boundary checkpoint.
